message.content:
**Short answer:** Yes – you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta. The city’s noise‑enforcement work is handled by the **Atlanta Police Department (APD)** and the **City’s Code Enforcement / Public Safety offices**, not directly by the city council. The council can pass ordinances that set the rules, but individual complaints are taken through the city’s 311 system or the APD. --- ## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta | Method | What to do | Contact | |--------|------------|---------| | **Online 311 portal** | • Go to the City of Atlanta’s 311 website:
• Select “Noise” or “Noise Complaint” from the list of services.
• Fill out the form with details (location, time, type of noise, etc.).
• Submit. | Online portal | | **Phone (311)** | • Call 311 (or 404‑656‑4000 if you’re outside the city).
• Tell the operator you want to file a noise complaint. | 404‑656‑4000 | | **Email** | • Send an email to **noise@atlantaga.gov** with the same details. | noise@atlantaga.gov | | **In person** | • Visit the **Atlanta Police Department** or the **City Hall** (City Clerk’s office) and request a noise‑complaint form. | City Hall, 55 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, Atlanta, GA 30303 | | **Mobile app** | • Download the **Atlanta 311** app (available on iOS and Android).
• Use the “Noise” service. | App store | ### What Information Should You Provide? 1. **Exact location** (street address or intersection). 2. **Time and date** of the noise. 3. **Description of the noise** (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs). 4. **Duration** (how long it lasted). 5. **Any prior attempts** to resolve the issue (e.g., talking to the neighbor). 6. **Your contact information** (optional but helpful for follow‑up). --- ## Atlanta’s Noise Ordinance (Key Points) - **Allowed noise levels** vary by zone (residential, commercial, industrial). - **Quiet hours**: 10 p.m.–7 a.m. on weekdays, 11 p.m.–7 a.m. on weekends. - **Construction**: Must be done between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. (except in certain zones). - **Music & parties**: Must not exceed 70 dB during quiet hours. - **Pet noise**: Dogs barking more than 3 minutes per hour may be cited. You can read the full ordinance here: --- ## What Happens After You File? 1. **APD or Code Enforcement** will review the complaint. 2. If the noise violates the ordinance, they may issue a citation or order the offending party to stop. 3. You’ll receive a **case number** and can track progress via the 311 portal or by calling 311. 4. If the issue persists, you can request a **formal investigation** or a **court hearing**. --- ## When to Contact the City Council - **Policy changes**: If you believe the current noise ordinance is inadequate or unfair, you can bring it to the attention of the **Atlanta City Council**. - **Public hearings**: The council holds public meetings where residents can voice concerns about noise issues. - **Council member office**: You can write to your local council member’s office to request a meeting or support for new ordinances. --- ### Quick Links - **Atlanta 311 portal**: - **Noise ordinance**: - **APD website**: - **City Hall address**: 55 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, Atlanta, GA 30303 --- **Bottom line:** You can definitely report a noise complaint to the City of Atlanta. Use the 311 system (online, phone, or in person), or email the noise department. The city council itself doesn’t handle individual complaints, but it can influence the rules that govern noise.
